items.title: Pressure stoichiometry
items.description: States or uses the relation that total pressure after decomposition equals P0 + x, where x is the pressure change of CH3CHO, consistent with 1 mole of acetaldehyde producing 2 moles of gaseous products.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference derives P_total = P0 + x from the stoichiometry CH3CHO → CH4 + CO.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misidentifies the pressure relation (e.g., P_total = P0 + 2x or P_total = P0 − x) obtains wrong x values and propagates errors through the entire solution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational stoichiometric relation; without it all downstream computations fail. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses P0+x relation explicitly.

items.title: x1 = 100 mmHg
items.description: Computes the pressure drop x1 = 100 mmHg for the experiment with initial pressure 400 mmHg and total pressure 500 mmHg after 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: when P0 = 400, after 100 sec, x = 100 (P0 + x = 500).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses P_total = P0 + 2x would obtain x1 = 50 instead of 100, corrupting all downstream calculations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate for rate and k calculations. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: x=100 for P0=400 stated.

items.title: x2 = 26 mmHg
items.description: Computes the pressure drop x2 = 26 mmHg for the experiment with initial pressure 200 mmHg and total pressure 226 mmHg after 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: when P0 = 200, after 100 sec, x = 26 (P0 + x = 226).
provenance.discriminates: A response that misapplies stoichiometry would obtain x2 = 13 or 52 instead of 26.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate for rate and k calculations. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: x=26 for P0=200 stated.

items.title: Rates r1 and r2
items.description: Computes the rates r1 = 1.0 mmHg/sec and r2 = 0.26 mmHg/sec by dividing each pressure drop by the time of 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: r1 = (300 − 400)/100 = 1, equivalently r1 = x1/t = 100/100 = 1.0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong time interval or miscalculates the rate would produce a different r1, affecting the order determination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate for order determination but follows directly from x values. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: r1=1 computed as 100/100.

items.title: Order formula
items.description: Applies the differential order formula n = log(r1/r2) / log(a1/a2) using initial pressures a1 = 400 and a2 = 200 as the concentration terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: n = ln(r1/r2) / ln(a1/a2) with a1 = 400 and a2 = 200.
provenance.discriminates: A response using remaining pressures (300 and 174) instead of initial pressures (400 and 200) as concentration terms would get n ≈ 2.5 instead of ≈ 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key method for determining order from two experiments. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Applies n=ln(r1/r2)/ln(a1/a2).

items.title: Order n ≈ 2
items.description: Reports the reaction order n as approximately 2 with respect to CH3CHO, the primary asked quantity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: n = ln(1/0.26)/ln(400/200) ≈ 1.94, rounded to 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response with incorrect intermediate values would produce a different order (e.g., 1.5 or 2.5).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the first sub-question; correctness collapses without it. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Reports n≈1.94, rounds to 2.

items.title: Second-order rate law
items.description: Applies the second-order integrated rate law k = (1/t) · x / [a(a − x)] for calculating the rate constant, where a is the initial pressure and (a − x) is the remaining pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses k = (1/t) · x / [a(a−x)], the second-order integrated rate law in pressure units.
provenance.discriminates: A response using the first-order law k = (1/t)·ln[a/(a−x)] or zero-order k = x/t would produce k values off by orders of magnitude with wrong units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct rate law selection is essential for k computation. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses k=(1/t)·x/[a(a−x)].

items.title: k1 and k2 from both experiments
items.description: Computes k1 = 8.33 × 10⁻⁶ and k2 = 7.47 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ separately from both experiments (P0 = 400 with remaining 300, and P0 = 200 with remaining 174) using t = 100 sec.

provenance.discriminates: A response using the wrong rate law or wrong x would obtain a different k1 value or different units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Both k values are required before averaging; merges both-experiments requirement. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: k1=8.33e-6 from experiment 1.

items.title: Average k = 7.9e-6
items.description: Reports the average rate constant k at 500°C as 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ obtained by averaging the k values from both experiments.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: k_av = 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports only one k value or an incorrect average would not match this final rate constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the second sub-question. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Average k=7.9e-6 reported.

items.title: T1 = 773 K
items.description: Converts the temperature 500°C to 773 K for use as T1 in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: T1 = 773 K (or 773.15 K) used in Arrhenius calculation.
provenance.discriminates: A response plugging 500 directly into the Arrhenius equation would obtain a nonsensical T2 ≈ 503 K.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Simple but necessary conversion for Arrhenius calculation. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses 773 K as T1.

items.title: Ea = 180000 J, R = 8.314
items.description: Converts activation energy of 180 kJ to 180000 J and uses R = 8.314 J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses 180000 in the Arrhenius calculation with R = 8.314.
provenance.discriminates: A response using Ea = 180 directly with R = 8.314 would produce a temperature essentially unchanged from T1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Unit-consistent parameters are required for correct Arrhenius result. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses 180000 J for Ea.

items.title: ln 2 as k ratio
items.description: Uses ln 2 as the ratio k2/k1 in the two-point Arrhenius equation, since the rate constant is to be twice its value at 500°C.

provenance.discriminates: A response using a different ratio (e.g., ln 1 = 0, or 2 instead of ln 2) would solve for a different T2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key setup for the temperature sub-question; incorrect ratio gives wrong T2. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: ln 2 used as k ratio.

items.title: T2 ≈ 793 K
items.description: Reports the final temperature T2 as approximately 793 K (≈ 520°C) at which the rate constant is twice its 500°C value.

provenance.discriminates: A response with a sign error in the Arrhenius equation would obtain T2 < 773 K, and one using Celsius or unconverted Ea would obtain entirely different values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers third sub-question; highest measured discrimination, caught 2/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: T2≈793 K (520°C) reported.

items.title: k units mmHg⁻¹s⁻¹
items.description: Avoids reporting the second-order rate constant k without units, correctly stating mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ consistent with pressure data used.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Rate-constant units mismatch': solvers may report k in s⁻¹ (first-order) or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ instead of mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response reporting k in s⁻¹ or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ units would be dimensionally inconsistent with the second-order pressure-based derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common unit pitfall for second-order pressure-based k; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: k units given as mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.

items.title: Unrounded n ≈ 1.94
items.description: Reports the unrounded value of the reaction order as approximately 1.94 (or 1.943) before rounding to 2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference reports n = 1.9434165 ≈ 2; the intermediate unrounded value confirms the differential method was actually applied.
provenance.discriminates: A response that simply states n = 2 without showing the computed value ~1.94 may have guessed the order rather than deriving it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth showing the raw computation result before rounding. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Reports 1.9434165 before rounding.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states the wavefunction 'is not unique to the observer' and 'is a tool that represents the information about the system known by the observer'; rollouts conveyed the idea but did not use this framing of non-uniqueness.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the wavefunction as a single objective physical entity shared by all observers.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct reference-answer claim with 0.50 measured discrimination; highest-importance concept.

validation.gold_why: Directly states wavefunction represents information known by observer, not unique to observer.

items.title: Unconditioned density matrix
items.description: Provides the unconditioned post-measurement density matrix (1/2)|↑↓⟩⟨↑↓| + (1/2)|↓↑⟩⟨↓↑| for an observer who knows a measurement occurred but not the outcome.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on this intermediate density matrix for the case of knowing a measurement happened without knowing the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates Observer 2's pure state with the unconditioned mixed state that arises when only the measurement occurrence is known.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests density matrices; 2/2 discrimination; gold=FAIL but genuinely necessary for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Unconditioned post-measurement density matrix not provided.

items.title: Measurement probabilities
items.description: States that measuring spin in the z-direction of one electron yields outcomes ↑ and ↓ each with probability 1/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that p(↑) = 1/2 and p(↓) = 1/2 for the z-basis measurement on the given state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the measurement has a determined outcome or different probabilities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supports the density-matrix discussion; 2/2 discrimination; intermediate technical result.

validation.gold_why: Measurement probabilities are not stated.

items.title: Avoids minus-sign switch
items.description: Avoids switching to a minus-sign singlet state in density matrix calculations after noting the triplet/singlet label discrepancy, instead using the plus-sign state as given throughout.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Minus-sign density matrix' pitfall (severity low) identifies the error of over-correcting by writing all subsequent density matrices with minus signs after identifying the label error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that notes the state is a triplet but then writes Observer 2's density matrix with minus signs on off-diagonal terms.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names a specific trap; 0/2 observed discrimination, so low weight; kept as a guard rail.

validation.gold_why: No minus-sign singlet state introduced; no switching occurs.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on this intermediate density matrix for the case of knowing a measurement happened without knowing the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates Observer 2's pure state with the unconditioned mixed state that arises when only the measurement occurrence is known.

validation.gold_why: Unconditioned post-measurement density matrix not provided.

items.title: IP final value
items.description: The response reports the ionization potential IP of X as 11.835 eV (or 11.84 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question a; reference gives a = 11.835 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving IP = 1.18 eV or 15.19 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; final requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: Reports a = IP = 11.835 eV.

items.title: EA final value
items.description: The response reports the electron affinity EA of X as 3.358 eV (or 3.36 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question b; reference gives b = 3.358 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving EA = 0.336 eV or 6.71 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; final requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: Reports b = EA = 3.358 eV.

items.title: Step 1 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 1 energy balance for the transfer of one electron between the two halves of X atoms as (N/2)×(IP − EA) = 409 kJ, with EA subtracted because electron attachment releases energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and correct rollouts use IP − EA for step 1; pitfall EA-sign-in-step-1 addresses the wrong move of adding EA.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 409 kJ or signs EA incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core equation for first sub-question; load-bearing for entire derivation.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a−b) = 409 kJ step; EA subtracted.

items.title: Step 2 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 2 energy balance for converting X⁻ ions to X⁺ as (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 733 kJ, because removing the extra electron costs +EA and ionizing the neutral costs +IP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses a + b for step 2; pitfall Step-2-electron-count and EA-sign-in-step-2 address the wrong moves.
provenance.discriminates: A response that models X⁻ → X⁺ as one-electron removal costing only IP, giving (N/2)×IP = 733 kJ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; core equation for second sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a+b) = 733 kJ step; EA added.

items.title: Two-electron step 2
items.description: The response states that converting each X⁻ ion to X⁺ requires removing two electrons, one reversing the electron affinity and one ionizing the neutral X atom.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Step 2 electron count', severity high.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats X⁻ → X⁺ as a single-electron transition costing only IP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key physical reasoning distinguishing step 2 from step 1.

validation.gold_why: States X⁻ loses two electrons: +EA then +IP.

items.title: Uses N/2 not N
items.description: The response uses N/2 = 3.0115×10²³ as the number of electron-transfer pairs in each energy-balance equation, not the full Avogadro's number N = 6.023×10²³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Using N instead of N/2', severity medium; reference uses N/2 throughout.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs full N into both equations, halving all per-atom eV values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical setup; though caught 0/2, using full N would halve all values.

validation.gold_why: Uses N/2 in both energy-balance equations.

items.title: kJ to J conversion
items.description: The response converts the given energies to joules as 409×10³ J and 733×10³ J before dividing by N/2 and converting to eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'kJ to J omitted', severity medium.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 409 and 733 directly in J, making final values too small by 1000×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary unit step; catching 0/2 but omission collapses all numeric results.

validation.gold_why: Uses 409×10³ and 733×10³ (J conversion).

items.title: eV conversion factor
items.description: The response uses the conversion 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J to convert per-atom joule energies into eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to obtain eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits this conversion or uses an incorrect factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required to produce answers in eV; reference answer uses this factor.

validation.gold_why: Divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to convert to eV.

items.title: IP minus EA equals 8.477
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP − EA = 8.477 eV from the 409 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; intermediate result directly leading to final values.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: IP plus EA equals 15.194

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; key intermediate for both final answers.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

items.title: Avoids exponent slip
items.description: Avoids writing the per-atom energy for the 409 kJ step as ~1.358×10⁻¹⁹ J; the correct per-atom value is ~1.358×10⁻¹⁸ J.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent in J/eV conversion', severity medium, observed in rollout 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response containing the off-by-10 exponent error that propagates to all final values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific arithmetic trap observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No per-atom value written incorrectly; correct method used.

items.title: Both quantities reported
items.description: The response reports both IP and EA values in eV, explicitly labelled, rather than stopping after solving only one of the two.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Only one quantity reported', severity low; answer format demands two labelled values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only IP or only EA.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question requests both quantities; ensures complete answer.

validation.gold_why: Reports both a (IP) and b (EA) in eV.

items.title: Simultaneous equations solved

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly solves the system to reach a = 11.835 and b = 3.358.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to combine the two balances into solved IP and EA values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination=1.00; the step that produces both final answers.

validation.gold_why: Solves simultaneous equations for a and b.

items.title: Semi-group nature of RG
items.description: The response describes the renormalization group as a semi-group, where the transformation renormalizes the system by decreasing the number of sites and has no inverse.

items.title: Avoid missing 1/2 factor
items.description: Avoids writing the decimation recursion relation as K' = ln cosh(2K) without the factor of 1/2 in the 1D Ising model.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Missing 1/2 factor': dropping the 1/2 yields spurious fixed points.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes K' = ln cosh(2K) instead of K' = (1/2) ln cosh(2K).
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; specific algebraic error in the derivation of coupling constants.

validation.gold_why: No incorrect formula without 1/2 factor written.

items.title: Avoid reversed flow direction
items.description: Avoids asserting that the renormalization group flow in the 1D Ising model goes toward strong coupling, whether by stating K' > K for finite positive K or by claiming K* = ∞ attracts while K* = 0 repels.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Flow direction reversed': correct is K' < K for all finite K>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the flow drives K to infinity for any initial K>0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Source 20 caught 2/2 negatives; merged with source 18 (1/2) covering same error.

validation.gold_why: No assertion that K' > K made.

items.title: Avoid finite-T transition claim
items.description: Avoids concluding that the 1D Ising model has a phase transition at a finite critical temperature T_c > 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Finite-T phase transition claimed': correct is no finite-T transition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports a finite-T phase transition based on a spurious fixed point.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; false phase transition claim is a key conceptual trap.

validation.gold_why: No finite-T transition claimed.

items.title: Avoid reversed flow direction
items.description: The response avoids asserting that K' > K for finite positive K in the 1D Ising model recursion relation, which would predict flow toward strong coupling.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Flow direction reversed': correct is K' < K for all finite K>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the flow drives K to infinity for any initial K>0.

validation.gold_why: No assertion that K' > K made.

items.title: General wave speed relation
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic relation v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} connecting the wave speed to the bulk modulus and volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on this starting formula; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to final answers without relating them to K and ρ, making the derivation uncheckable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate formula; discrimination 0/2 but genuinely necessary for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} as general acoustic relation.

items.title: General impedance relation
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic impedance relation Z = (Kρ)^{1/2}, equivalently Z = ρv, connecting impedance to bulk modulus and density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} = ρv; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both impedance results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted impedance formula such as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate formula; discrimination 0/2 but genuinely necessary for correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} as general impedance relation.

items.title: Adiabatic index definition
items.description: The response defines γ = C_P/C_V = (C_V + 1)/C_V and states that γ > 1 for the ideal classical gas with temperature-independent specific heat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts correctly identified γ = C_P/C_V > 1, and this is load-bearing for the adiabatic results and the comparison between limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses γ ≤ 1 or never defines γ, making the comparison between limits unjustified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for correctness of adiabatic results; discrimination 0/2 but no near-duplicate covers it.

validation.gold_why: Defines γ = C_P/C_V and states γ > 1.

items.title: Adiabatic exceeds isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2} (i.e., v_S/v_T = γ^{1/2} and Z_S/Z_T = γ^{1/2}), because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; highest discrimination item, captures the key comparison.

validation.gold_why: States adiabatic v and Z are larger than isothermal by γ>1.

items.title: Frequency-regime identification
items.description: The response identifies the adiabatic limit as achieved at higher wave frequencies because the oscillation period is too short for heat exchange, and the isothermal limit as the low-frequency regime where the period is long enough for temperature to equilibrate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Frequency–regime reversal' (severity high): inverting which limit corresponds to high vs low frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the frequency assignments, saying fast oscillations allow temperature equilibration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers final sub-question; caught 1/2 negatives, absorbs frequency-reversal pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Correctly assigns adiabatic to high frequency, isothermal to low.

items.title: Isothermal equation of state
items.description: The response uses the ideal-gas equation of state P = NT/V (or equivalently P = nT) under isothermal conditions to derive the isothermal bulk modulus K = P.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states P = NT/V at X = T = const and differentiates to get K = P; this is the load-bearing step for the isothermal case.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states K = P without connecting it to the ideal-gas equation of state under constant temperature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing derivation step; caught 1/2 negatives, anchors K = P in first principles.

validation.gold_why: Uses P = NT/V under isothermal conditions to derive K = P.

items.title: Adiabatic PV-gamma relation
items.description: The response uses the adiabatic relation P ∝ V^{−γ} (i.e., PV^γ = const) to derive the adiabatic bulk modulus K = γP.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly writes P = fV^{−γ} and performs differentiation to obtain K = γP; this is the load-bearing step distinguishing the adiabatic case.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states K = γP without any thermodynamic justification from the adiabatic P–V relation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing derivation step; caught 1/2 negatives, anchors K = γP in thermodynamics.

validation.gold_why: Uses P = fV^{−γ} to derive K = γP.

items.title: Compression independence
items.description: The response notes that the isothermal wave speed v = (T/m)^{1/2} does not depend on the static compression or ambient pressure of the gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states 'v does not depend on the static compression of the gas,' a physical observation no attempt made.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats v_T as depending on ambient pressure or density changes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added physical insight from reference; caught 1/2 negatives, low importance.

validation.gold_why: Notes isothermal v does not depend on static compression.

items.title: Avoid impedance errors
items.description: Avoids writing the wave impedance as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv) instead of Z = ρv = (Kρ)^{1/2}, and avoids computing only wave speeds while omitting both impedances.

provenance.discriminates: A response that reports impedance values with wrong units and wrong density dependence.

validation.gold_why: Uses Z = (Kρ)^{1/2}, not inverted forms.

items.title: Probability as overlap
items.description: The response identifies the probability of getting energy eigenvalue E_k as the squared modulus of the overlap P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(t)⟩|², where ⟨E_k| is the energy eigenstate and |ψ(t)⟩ is the time-evolved state.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts begin from P(E_k,t) = |⟨k|ψ(t)⟩|² as the measurement postulate before substituting U(t).
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes |⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² without connecting it to the measurement postulate |⟨k|ψ(t)⟩|².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key Born-rule step; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Opens with probability as |⟨E_k|ψ(t)⟩|².

items.title: Probability via U(t)
items.description: The response writes the probability expression using the time-evolution operator as |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² by substituting |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks to use U(t) to derive an expression for P(E_k, t); the target expression is |⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the final |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|² without ever exhibiting the intermediate probability expression containing U(t).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly demands U(t); caught 1/2 negatives, core derivation step.

validation.gold_why: Boxed expression contains |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|².

items.title: Final expression boxed
items.description: The response states and boxes the final probability expression P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|², showing that the time-dependent phase has modulus squared equal to 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target is the time-independent expression; the reference answer boxes |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes verbally without writing the explicit final probability formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final result; caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination, essential correctness.

validation.gold_why: Final expression |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² is boxed.

items.title: Concludes time-independent
items.description: The response explicitly concludes that the probability expression is independent of time, either by stating dP(E_k,t)/dt = 0 or by declaring that no time-dependent factor survives.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to show the expression is independent of time; the final conclusion must be stated explicitly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|² but never states that this means the probability is time-independent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the question; caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Equality chain ends with no time-dependent factor surviving.

items.title: General initial state
items.description: The response carries out the derivation for a general initial state |ψ(0)⟩ using the time-evolution operator, obtaining an expression for the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue rather than only the special case |ψ(0)⟩ = |E_k⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The eigenstate-only proof pitfall (severity medium) warns against proving the result only for the trivial case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.
provenance.discriminates: A response that proves P = 1 for |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩ and generalizes without showing the derivation for an arbitrary state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Guards against trivial special case; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Expression uses general |ψ(0)⟩, not special case.

items.title: Avoids z·z for |z|²
items.description: Avoids evaluating |e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}|² for the particular energy eigenvalue as e^{-iE_k t/ℏ} · e^{-iE_k t/ℏ} = e^{-2iE_k t/ℏ}, instead using the complex conjugate e^{+iE_k t/ℏ} to obtain 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Complex conjugate in |·|²' pitfall (severity high) identifies the specific error of computing z·z instead of zz*.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mechanically squares the phase without conjugation, yielding a spurious time-dependent factor e^{-2iE_k t/ℏ}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed algebraic mistake; caught 1/2 negatives, specific and checkable.

validation.gold_why: No erroneous z·z computation present.

items.title: Final expression boxed
items.description: The response states the final probability expression P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² (or |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|²) and presents it in a boxed expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target is the time-independent expression; the reference answer boxes |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes verbally without writing the explicit final probability formula.

validation.gold_why: Final expression |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² is boxed.

items.title: Part ii rate 9 times

items.title: Part ii 3B squared

items.title: Part ii A unchanged

items.title: Part iii rate 8 times

items.description: Part (iii) shows the new rate expression substituting [2A]^1 and [2B]^2 to derive the factor of 8 times.

items.title: Part iii factors multiplied

provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes multiply vs add; caught 1/2 negatives.

items.title: Part iii A factor 2

items.title: Avoid swapped exponents
items.description: Avoids writing the differential rate equation as k[A]^2[B]^1, which transposes the reaction order given for A and B.

provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a linear denominator, drops the square root, or places E−E_s outside the sqrt.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination but the sqrt spectral denominator is essential to the correct expression.

validation.gold_why: Denominator contains J√(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²)

items.title: Theta difference form
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains the Heaviside theta function factor θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) or an equivalent form such as θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverge on the exact form: θ(4J²−(E−E_s)²), θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|), or θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t); all are equivalent for J>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a single θ with the wrong argument or a difference with reversed ordering.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; the theta support factor is a required deliverable of the question.

validation.gold_why: θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) present in expression

items.title: Substitution x = ka
items.description: The derivation uses the substitution x = ka with dk = dx/a, by which the integral limits are transformed from [−π/a, π/a] to [−π, π].

provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational step for cancelling a; no measured discrimination but enables correct prefactor.

items.title: Root equation
items.description: The derivation identifies the roots of the delta function argument by solving cos(ka) = (E_s − E)/(2J).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific intermediate equation; grounded in the delta function root condition.

items.title: Two symmetric roots
items.description: The derivation accounts for both symmetric roots ±k₀ of the delta function argument within [−π/a, π/a], each contributing a factor 1/|g'(k_i)| to the integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Counting only one root' (severity high): forgetting the second root at −k₀ halves the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies only k₀ = arccos[−(E−E_s)/(2J)] and misses −k₀, yielding N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)) instead of 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; two-root counting is a key intermediate with real discriminative power.

validation.gold_why: Expression accounts for both roots symmetrically

items.title: Delta identity
items.description: The derivation applies the identity δ(g(k)) = Σ_i δ(k−k_i)/|g'(k_i)|, by which the integral of the delta function is transformed into a sum over roots.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core transformation identity; explains how the delta integral becomes a discrete sum.

items.title: Jacobian derivative
items.description: The derivation computes the Jacobian |g'(k)| = 2Ja|sin(ka)| from the derivative of the 2J cos(ka) term in the delta function argument.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific intermediate derivative; enables the correct Jacobian factor in the final expression.

items.title: sin² substitution
items.description: The derivation substitutes sin²(k₀a) = 1 − ((E−E_s)/(2J))² to express the Jacobian factor in terms of E, E_s, and J.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key algebraic step linking k-space to E-space; grounds the sqrt denominator.

items.title: Band edges
items.description: The derivation identifies the band edges E_b = E_s − 2|J| and E_t = E_s + 2|J|, where cos(ka) = ±1 and the sqrt(4J²−(E−E_s)²) denominator vanishes.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific band-edge values; define the theta function arguments in the final expression.

items.title: Support to theta
items.description: The derivation explains that the Heaviside theta function arises because the roots of the delta function argument exist only when |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J|, so the integral evaluates to zero outside this range.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the 'explain' part; theta arises from root existence condition.

items.title: Factor of 2 from roots
items.description: The derivation combines the two root contributions to obtain an overall factor of 2 in the expression for n(E).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate factor from combining two roots; contributes to the correct prefactor.

items.title: Avoids spurious factor of a
items.description: Avoids retaining a spurious factor of the lattice constant a in the final expression for n(E) by correctly applying the substitution dk = dx/a.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Failing to cancel lattice constant a' (severity medium): Na/π retains an extra a if dk=dx/a is overlooked.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose final expression has 2Na/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)) instead of 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; a real pitfall that would introduce a dimensionful extra factor.

validation.gold_why: No spurious factor of a retained

items.title: Avoids wrong ordering
items.description: Avoids the wrong band-edge ordering in the theta function expression θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) where E_b > E_t for J > 0, which would yield a negative density of states.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong band-edge ordering' (severity medium): the reference uses E_b, E_t without defining them, and the bottom/top assignment depends on the sign of J.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines E_b = E_s + 2J and E_t = E_s − 2J for J > 0, reversing the step-function difference and giving a negative DOS.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; wrong ordering gives negative DOS, a sign-error trap.

validation.gold_why: Uses standard θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) form

items.title: Complete final expression
items.description: The final expression for n(E) combines the spectral prefactor N/(πJ·sqrt(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²)) with the theta function support factor θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires the correct closed-form n(E); the reference answer has prefactor N/π with no extra a.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves Na/π or any incorrect prefactor in the final n(E).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Synthesis criterion; verifies the final expression assembles prefactor and support factor correctly.

validation.gold_why: N/π present in prefactor after a cancels

items.title: Bromwich inversion formula
items.description: Writes the Bromwich inversion formula for inverting the Laplace transform to obtain g(E) as g(E) = (1/2πi) ∫_{β'-i∞}^{β'+i∞} dβ e^{+βE} Q(β) with a positive sign in the exponent.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly provides this formula with β' notation and the e^{+βE} kernel.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the formula with e^{-βE} (copying the forward transform sign) or omits the 1/(2πi) prefactor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result; caught 1/2 flawed responses, highest measured discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Bromwich formula written exactly with positive exponent.

items.title: Q as Laplace transform
items.description: Identifies the partition function Q(β) = ∫_0^∞ dE e^{-βE} g(E) as the Laplace transform of the density of states g(E), recognizing this integral as a forward Laplace transform.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly identified this relationship; it is the foundational step the entire derivation depends on.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the integral as a Fourier transform or fails to connect it to the Laplace transform structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Conceptual foundation of the derivation; 0/2 discrimination but genuinely necessary.

validation.gold_why: Identifies Q as Laplace transform of g(E).

items.title: Harmonic oscillator Q(β)
items.description: States the quantum harmonic oscillator partition function as Q(β) = e^{-βℏω/2}/(1 - e^{-βℏω}) or an equivalent closed form.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required input for the HO-specific derivation; question explicitly asks for harmonic oscillator.

items.title: β variable significance
items.description: Explains the significance of the variables in the equation, identifying β as the inverse temperature β = 1/(k_B T).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses the variable-significance sub-question with a specific physical identification.

items.title: E variable significance
items.description: Explains the significance of the variables in the equation, identifying E as the energy of the harmonic oscillator system.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses variable-significance sub-question; basic but explicitly requested by the question.

items.title: g(E) variable significance
items.description: Explains the significance of g(E) as the density of states, representing the number of accessible states per unit energy interval.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses variable significance; g(E) is the central quantity being derived.

items.title: Q(β) variable significance
items.description: Explains the significance of Q(β) as the canonical partition function encoding the thermodynamic properties of the harmonic oscillator.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses variable significance; Q(β) is the starting point of the derivation.

items.title: Bromwich contour and analyticity
items.description: Specifies that the Bromwich inversion contour runs vertically from β' - i∞ to β' + i∞ in the complex β-plane, with β' placed to the right of all singularities so that Q(β) is analytic in the region to the right of the contour.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing contour placement condition for valid inversion; specific complex-analysis detail.

items.title: Residue theorem role
items.description: Discusses the role of complex analysis, specifically the residue theorem, in evaluating the Bromwich integral by summing residues at the poles of Q(β).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses the sub-question on the role of complex analysis; specific technique.

items.title: Delta-comb density of states
items.description: Obtains the density of states for the quantum harmonic oscillator as a series of delta functions g(E) = Σ_n δ(E - E_n) at the energy eigenvalues E_n = (n + 1/2)ℏω.

provenance.calibration_rationale: The derivation's end result for the HO; specific and directly checkable.

items.title: Pole-energy correspondence
items.description: Recognizes that the poles of Q(β) in the complex β-plane directly correspond to the energy eigenvalues of the harmonic oscillator.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key physical insight connecting complex analysis to the spectrum; derivation-relevant.

items.title: Classical limit connection
items.description: Notes that in the high-temperature classical limit where k_B T ≫ ℏω, the quantum delta-function comb for the harmonic oscillator approximates the flat classical density of states 1/(ℏω).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Added physical depth bridging quantum and classical results; not strictly required.

items.title: Correct pole locations
items.description: Avoids placing the poles of Q(β) for the harmonic oscillator at real-axis locations β_n = 2πn/(ℏω) or at β_n = i·2πin/(ℏω) with a spurious extra factor of i.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Pole locations of Q(β)' (severity high): foreseen error of mis-solving e^{-βℏω}=1 with wrong placement.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes poles on the real axis or with β_n = -2πn/(ℏω), producing delta functions at incorrect energies.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed error in 1/2 flawed responses; specific sign and formula trap.

validation.gold_why: No incorrect pole locations given.

items.title: Quantum result required
items.description: Avoids presenting only the classical flat density of states 1/(ℏω) as the complete answer for the harmonic oscillator without acknowledging the quantum delta-function comb.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Classical–quantum conflation' (severity medium): the classical result is simpler but incomplete if the quantum spectrum is expected.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives g(E) = 1/(ℏω) as the sole final answer without mentioning quantized energy levels.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but addresses a real conceptual trap specific to the HO.

validation.gold_why: No classical-only answer presented.

items.title: Complex analysis required
items.description: Avoids inverting Q(β) by a purely term-by-term series expansion without any reference to complex analysis, contour integration, or the residue theorem.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Series approach evades complex analysis': the series method is valid but does not address sub-question (c) about the role of complex analysis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that expands Q(β) = Σ e^{-βε_n} and identifies each term as a delta function, with no mention of the Bromwich contour or residues.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination; directly tied to the question's explicit ask about complex analysis.

validation.gold_why: Uses complex analysis, not series expansion alone.

items.title: Equal-concentration simplification
items.description: States that because the initial concentrations of the two reactants are equal and stoichiometry is 1:1, [A] remains equal to [B] throughout the reaction, enabling use of the simplified second-order rate law rate = k[A]^2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Load-bearing simplification required by the reference answer to reduce the mixed second-order rate law to simple second-order form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the general mixed-order formula without recognizing the equal-concentration edge case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key conceptual step that enables the entire calculation.

validation.gold_why: States concentrations start equal and remain equal throughout.

items.title: Second order overall
items.description: Identifies the reaction as second order overall, since it is first order with respect to each reactant.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts recognize the overall second-order nature of the reaction before applying the integrated law.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the reaction as first order overall.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; recognizing overall order underpins the integrated law choice.

validation.gold_why: States reaction treated as simple second order.

items.title: Integrated rate law plus sign
items.description: Writes the integrated rate law for this reaction as 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 + kt with the plus sign before the kt term.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all correct rollouts and the reference answer uses the form 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 + kt.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 - kt, producing an increasing concentration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the correct formula with plus sign is essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Writes 1/[A] = kt + 1/[A_0] with correct values.

items.title: Correct input values
items.description: Uses [A]_0 = 0.100 M, k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} L mol^{-1} s^{-1}, and t = 100 s as the inputs in the integrated rate law computation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value of k must appear in the response's calculation to reach the correct answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that alters the value of k (e.g., treating it as a first-order constant with different units).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged items caught 0–1/2; correct numeric inputs are necessary but less discriminating.

validation.gold_why: Uses k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} in calculation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference compute 1/[A]_0 = 10.0 L/mol as an intermediate value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mishandles the reciprocal of 0.100 M.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate value for the final sum.

validation.gold_why: Shows 1/0.100 mol, sum implies 10.0 L/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus value among all correct rollouts; reference also yields kt = 1.0 L/mol.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes kt as 0.01, 0.1, or 10.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; required intermediate whose value directly feeds the sum.

validation.gold_why: Shows kt term; sum of 11 implies kt = 1.0.

items.title: Sum equals 11
items.description: Computes 1/[A] = 10.0 + 1.0 = 11 L/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference obtain 1/[A] = 11 L/mol before taking the reciprocal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that sums to a different value (e.g., 9.0, 10.1, 11.0 reported as final answer).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the summed reciprocal is the direct precursor to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states = 11 L/mol.

items.title: Final concentration 0.091 M
items.description: Reports the concentration of A remaining after 100 s as the reciprocal of 11 L/mol, i.e., [A] = 0.091 M (accepting 0.0909 M or equivalent rounding).

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the required final deliverable: concentration of A remaining after 100 s.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 11 M or 11 L/mol as the concentration, or that gives 0.037 M from a first-order law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; the requested final quantity, absorbing the reciprocal-mistake pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Reports [A] = 0.091 M.

items.title: Units of M
items.description: States the final concentration of A with units of M (mol/L).

provenance.evidence_detail: Question demands the concentration of A remaining, with implied units of M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits units or reports L/mol as the final concentration unit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; real but minor depth item on unit reporting.

validation.gold_why: Final answer given as 0.091 M.

items.title: Avoid first-order misapplication
items.description: Avoids using the first-order integrated law ln[A] = ln[A]_0 - kt with k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} as a pseudo-first-order constant, which would yield approximately 0.0368 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall: 'First-order law misapplied'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misreads 'first order with respect to each reactant' as 'first order overall'.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; common order-misidentification trap observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No first-order integrated law used.

items.title: Avoid sign reversal
items.description: Avoids writing 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 - kt, which would give 1/[A] = 9.0 L/mol and [A] = 0.111 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall: 'Sign reversed in rate law'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that subtracts kt from 1/[A]_0 instead of adding it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; sign error produces a plausible but wrong answer.

validation.gold_why: Uses plus sign before kt term.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific sign error in reservoir entropy derivation.

items.title: UU† identity
items.description: The response uses det(\hat{U}\hat{U}^\dagger) = \det \hat{1} = 1 as the starting identity for determining the determinant of a unitary matrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows the chain det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 and det U† = (det U)* leading to |det U|² = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without connecting it to the unitary condition UU† = I.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundation of the proof; zero measured discrimination but no correctness without it.

validation.gold_why: Derives from det(UU†)=1 and det U†=(det U)*.

items.title: Determinant multiplicativity
items.description: The response uses det(\hat{U}\hat{U}^\dagger) = \det \hat{U} \cdot \det \hat{U}^\dagger to separate the product determinant.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows the chain det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 and det U† = (det U)* leading to |det U|² = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without connecting it to the unitary condition UU† = I.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; zero measured discrimination but load-bearing for the proof.

validation.gold_why: Derives from det(UU†)=1 and det U†=(det U)*.

items.title: Conjugate determinant
items.description: The response states and uses the property det \hat{U}^\dagger = (\det \hat{U})^*.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly shows the chain det(UU†) = det 1 = 1 and det U† = (det U)* leading to |det U|² = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without connecting it to the unitary condition UU† = I.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required to connect UU† to |det U|²; zero measured discrimination but essential step.

validation.gold_why: Derives from det(UU†)=1 and det U†=(det U)*.

items.title: Modulus-one determinant
items.description: The response concludes |\det \hat{U}|^2 = 1, equivalently \det \hat{U} = e^{i\alpha} where \alpha is a real number.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the general constraint on det(U) for a unitary matrix; the reference derives |det U|² = 1 and det U = e^{iα}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a wrong modulus (e.g., det U = 1) or omits the general property entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result for sub-question 1; zero measured discrimination but answer is wrong without it.

validation.gold_why: States |det U|² = 1 explicitly.

items.title: Exponential identity
items.description: The response states \det(\exp(i\hat{F})) = \exp(i \operatorname{Tr} \hat{F}) for the operator \hat{U} = \exp(i\hat{F}).

provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong identity such as det(exp(A)) = exp(det A) or det(exp(A)) = Tr(exp A).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result for sub-question 2; zero measured discrimination but central to the explicit calculation.

validation.gold_why: States det U = exp(i Tr F).

items.title: Spectrum to trace
items.description: The response connects the known spectrum of \hat{F} to \operatorname{Tr} \hat{F} = \sum_k \lambda_k, which enters the determinant formula via \exp(i \operatorname{Tr} \hat{F}).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to calculate det(U) explicitly for U = exp(iF); the reference gives det U = exp(i Tr F).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong identity such as det(exp(A)) = exp(det A) or det(exp(A)) = Tr(exp A).

validation.gold_why: States det U = exp(i Tr F).

items.title: Correct scalar c
items.description: The response gives c = e^{-i\alpha/N} where N is the rank of the matrix \hat{U}.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Highest-discrimination item: caught 2/2 flawed responses, central to sub-question 3.

validation.gold_why: Gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank.

items.title: Rank N identified
items.description: The response identifies N as the rank (dimension) of the matrix \hat{U}, not an arbitrary parameter.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to prove existence of c such that det(U') = 1; the reference gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank (dimension).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives c = e^{-iα} (missing the 1/N factor) or c = e^{+iα/N} (wrong sign).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Keeps the scalar formula well-defined; strong source discrimination (2/2) supports this grouping.

validation.gold_why: Gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank.

items.title: Determinant scaling
items.description: The response uses det(c\hat{U}) = c^N \det \hat{U} when computing the determinant of the transformed matrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing dimension factor in det(cU)', severity high: the Nth power is easy to overlook.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key step to reach det U'=1; source caught 1/2 negatives, moderate discrimination.

items.title: Unimodular result
items.description: The response shows \det \hat{U}' = 1 for the transform \hat{U}' = e^{-i\alpha/N}\hat{U}, yielding a unimodular matrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to prove existence of c such that det(U') = 1; the reference gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank (dimension).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives c = e^{-iα} (missing the 1/N factor) or c = e^{+iα/N} (wrong sign).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final result of sub-question 3; source caught 2/2 negatives, highest discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank.

items.title: Phase cancellation
items.description: The response shows that c^N \cdot \det \hat{U} = e^{-i\alpha} \cdot e^{i\alpha} = 1, hence completing the proof that \det \hat{U}' = 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to prove existence of c such that det(U') = 1; the reference gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank (dimension).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives c = e^{-iα} (missing the 1/N factor) or c = e^{+iα/N} (wrong sign).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Closing algebraic step; source caught 2/2 but this sub-step is intermediate rather than standalone.

validation.gold_why: Gives c = e^{-iα/N} with N the rank.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the general constraint on det(U) for a unitary matrix; the reference derives |det U|² = 1 and det U = e^{iα}.

items.title: Hermitian real trace
items.description: The response notes that \hat{F} being Hermitian means its eigenvalues are real, so \operatorname{Tr} \hat{F} is real and \exp(i \operatorname{Tr} \hat{F}) is a pure phase e^{i\alpha}.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to calculate det(U) explicitly for U = exp(iF); the reference gives det U = exp(i Tr F).

validation.gold_why: States det U = exp(i Tr F).

items.title: Avoids linear det scaling
items.description: Avoids writing det(c\hat{U}) = c \cdot \det(\hat{U}) instead of det(c\hat{U}) = c^N \cdot \det(\hat{U}) when computing the determinant of the scaled matrix.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing dimension factor in det(cU)', severity high: the Nth power is easy to overlook.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses c·det(U) and obtains c = e^{-iα} (no Nth root).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed error; source caught 1/2 negatives, moderate discrimination on a specific wrong move.

validation.gold_why: Uses c = e^{-iα/N}, not c alone, correctly.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed error; source caught 1/2 negatives, directly sabotages the unimodular result.

validation.gold_why: Uses negative exponent e^{-iα/N}, correct sign.

items.title: Pressure ratio orientation
items.description: Computes the pressure ratio as 760 torr divided by 591.6 torr, placing 760 in the numerator and 591.6 in the denominator.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; correct ratio orientation is a key intermediate prone to inversion.

items.title: N+1 states no degeneracy
items.description: States that at thermal equilibrium the chain has only N+1 configurations with n = 0, 1, ..., N left links open and the rest closed, each with energy E_n = nΔ and a single microstate with no binomial degeneracy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires calculating ⟨n⟩; identifying the correct state space (N+1 states, no degeneracy) is the load-bearing first step that all consensus rollouts agreed on.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that treat the N links as independent two-state systems with 2^N configurations or C(N,n) degeneracy, which would produce a Fermi-Dirac-like result instead of the correct geometric-series partition function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; foundation of the entire model, without which the partition function is wrong.

validation.gold_why: States N+1 states with energy nΔ, single microstate each.

items.title: Gibbs probability W_n
items.description: Writes the Gibbs distribution probability W_n = e^{−nΔ/T}/Z for the state with n open links.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes W_n = (1/Z) exp{−nΔ/T} using Eqs. (2.58) and (2.59); all rollouts agree.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that assign equal probability to all states, or that use a degeneracy factor C(N,n) in the probability weight.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; key intermediate step anchoring the statistical-mechanics derivation.

validation.gold_why: Writes W_n = e^{-nΔ/T}/Z.

items.title: Geometric partition function
items.description: Writes the partition function as the geometric progression Z = Σ_{n=0}^{N} e^{−nΔ/T} = (1 − λ^{N+1})/(1 − λ) with parameter λ = e^{−Δ/T} < 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree on Z = (1−λ^{N+1})/(1−λ) with λ = e^{-Δ/T}.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that write Z = (1−λ^N)/(1−λ) (off-by-one, dropping the n=N term) or Z = (1+e^{-Δ/T})^N (independent links).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; load-bearing intermediate result needed for every downstream formula.

validation.gold_why: Writes geometric progression with λ=e^{-Δ/T}<1.

items.title: Ratio form of average
items.description: Expresses the average number of open links as the ratio ⟨n⟩ = Σ_{n=1}^{N} n e^{−nΔ/T} / Σ_{n=0}^{N} e^{−nΔ/T} before evaluating the closed form.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes ⟨n⟩ = Σ n W_n = [Σ n e^{-nΔ/T}] / [Σ e^{-nΔ/T}] as an intermediate step before computing the geometric sums.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that jump to the final answer without showing the ensemble average construction from the Gibbs distribution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; required intermediate connecting the Gibbs probability to the exact formula.

validation.gold_why: Expresses ⟨n⟩ as ratio of sums before closed form.

items.title: Derivative trick
items.description: Computes the numerator sum Σ_{n=1}^{N} n λ^n using the derivative relation λ d/dλ Σ_{n=0}^{N} λ^n with parameter λ = e^{−Δ/T}.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and all rollouts use λ ∂/∂λ to evaluate the weighted sum; the reference explicitly writes λ ∂/∂λ [(1−λ^{N+1})/(1−λ)].
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that compute d/dλ[Σ λ^n] without the prefactor λ, which would introduce an erroneous factor of e^{Δ/T} into the result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; the specific mathematical step that yields the exact closed-form result.

validation.gold_why: Uses λ d/dλ derivative trick for numerator.

items.title: Exact formula for ⟨n⟩
items.description: Gives the exact formula ⟨n⟩ = 1/(e^{Δ/T} − 1) − (N+1)/(e^{(N+1)Δ/T} − 1).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference give this exact closed-form expression (Eq. (**)).
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that drop the second term (N+1)/(e^{(N+1)Δ/T}−1), which would diverge as T/Δ at high temperature instead of saturating at N/2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; the central quantitative result of the entire calculation.

validation.gold_why: Exact formula given in equation (**).

items.title: Low-temperature limit
items.description: Gives the low-temperature limit ⟨n⟩ ≈ e^{−Δ/T} ≪ 1 for T ≪ Δ, approximately independently of N.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree on this limit; the reference explicitly shows the second term is negligible for N > 1.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim the second term (N+1)e^{-(N+1)Δ/T} dominates at low T, or that give a different low-T scaling such as e^{-NΔ/T}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.5; essential temperature-dependence result, though one flawed response also got it.

validation.gold_why: States low-T limit e^{-Δ/T}, independent of N.

items.title: High-temperature limit N/2
items.description: Gives the high-temperature limit ⟨n⟩ ≈ N/2 for T ≫ (N+1)Δ, where both terms in the exact formula become large and mostly cancel.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree that ⟨n⟩ → N/2 at high temperature, where each link has equal probability of being open or closed.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give N or N/2 − 1 as the high-T limit, or that claim ⟨n⟩ diverges without bound.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; key asymptotic result whose derivation requires careful Taylor expansion.

validation.gold_why: States high-T limit ⟨n⟩≈N/2.

items.title: High-T condition (N+1)Δ
items.description: States that the high-temperature limit requires T to exceed both Δ and (N+1)Δ, not merely T ≫ Δ.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states: 'If T is much larger than both Δ and (N+1)Δ' as the condition for the N/2 limit.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that state T ≫ Δ alone is sufficient for the N/2 saturation, which would incorrectly apply the high-T limit in the intermediate regime.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; the condition on (N+1)Δ is a subtle point many responses get wrong.

validation.gold_why: Requires T≫Δ and (N+1)Δ for high-T limit.

items.title: High-T equal probability
items.description: States that at high temperature the energy cost Δ is negligible so each link has approximately equal probability of being open or closed.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'at very high temperatures, the energy gain Δ is negligible, and each link has an equal chance to be open or closed.'
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give the N/2 limit numerically but do not explain the physical basis in terms of Δ becoming negligible relative to T.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.5; physical picture of the high-temperature regime, adds depth beyond the formula.

validation.gold_why: States Δ negligible, equal open/closed probability.

items.title: Intermediate regime T/Δ
items.description: Identifies the intermediate temperature regime ⟨n⟩ ≈ T/Δ valid for Δ ≪ T ≪ NΔ when N ≫ 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference identify this linear regime, which the reference derives from the first term having reached T/Δ while the second remains negligible.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give only two regimes (low-T and high-T) and miss the broad intermediate window where ⟨n⟩ grows linearly with T.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.5; the broad-temperature linear regime is central to the N ≫ 1 analysis.

validation.gold_why: Identifies ⟨n⟩≈T/Δ for Δ≪T≪(N+1)Δ.

items.title: Crossover scale NΔ
items.description: States that the crossover temperature scale between linear growth T/Δ and saturation at N/2 occurs at T ~ NΔ.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference identify T ~ NΔ (or equivalently (N+1)Δ) as the scale where the second term transitions from negligible to important.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that place the crossover at T ~ Δ, missing the N-dependence of the saturation scale.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.5; names the specific crossover scale that anchors the full temperature-dependence picture.

validation.gold_why: Crossover at T~(N+1)Δ implied by regime boundaries.

items.title: Physical interpretation T/Δ
items.description: Provides the physical interpretation that thermal agitation with characteristic energy T ≫ Δ opens on average T/Δ links but not more.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'the thermal agitation with the characteristic energy T ≫ Δ is sufficient to open, on average, T/Δ left links of the chain, but not more than that.'
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that derive the T/Δ scaling mathematically but do not connect it to the physical picture of thermal energy opening links.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; the physical reasoning behind the intermediate regime formula.

validation.gold_why: Gives physical interpretation of T/Δ links opened.

items.title: Large-N limit form
items.description: States that for N ≫ 1 the second term becomes negligible and ⟨n⟩ approaches 1/(e^{Δ/T} − 1), the Bose–Einstein form.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts note the large-N limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.0; the large-N simplification connecting the zipper model to a recognizable statistical form.

validation.gold_why: Second term negligible for N≫1, approaches Bose-Einstein form.

items.title: Avoids wrong linearization
items.description: Avoids applying the high-temperature linearization e^{Δ/T} − 1 ≈ Δ/T in the low-temperature regime T ≪ Δ where e^{Δ/T} is exponentially large rather than close to 1.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap: misapplying the Taylor expansion outside its regime yields ⟨n⟩ ≈ T/Δ instead of e^{−Δ/T}.

items.title: D* max momentum
items.description: The maximum momentum of the D∗− in the laboratory is stated as approximately 0.54 GeV/c (or equivalently ~550 MeV/c).

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer gives p_D* = 0.54 GeV/c; consensus of rollouts gives ~549–550 MeV/c.
provenance.discriminates: A response that miscalculates the D* momentum or leaves it unevaluated.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final answer for first sub-question; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: States 0.54 GeV/c for D*.

items.title: Pion max momentum
items.description: The maximum momentum of the π− in the laboratory is stated as approximately 79 MeV/c (or equivalently ~80 MeV/c).

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer gives p_π = 79 MeV/c; consensus of rollouts gives ~79.9 MeV/c.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports the unboosted rest-frame momentum p* ≈ 39 MeV/c or a wrongly boosted value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final answer for second sub-question; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States 79 MeV/c for pion.

items.title: Colliding-beam frame
items.description: The response identifies that for a colliding beam at c.m. energy 4.03 GeV, the laboratory frame coincides with the c.m. frame so the maximum D∗− momentum equals its c.m. two-body momentum.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing assumption: without it the maximum momentum concept changes entirely.

items.title: Two-body momentum formula
items.description: The momentum of the D∗− is computed using the two-body c.m. frame formula p = √[(s−(m₁+m₂)²)(s−(m₁−m₂)²)]/(2√s) with the produced meson masses.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Formula that produces the 0.54 GeV/c value; untested but essential intermediate step.

items.title: s from c.m. energy
items.description: The squared c.m. energy s = (4.03 GeV)² is used as the input to the production kinematics calculation.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Simple but anchors the starting value; untested, low weight.

items.title: Production masses used
items.description: The D⁺ mass 1868.3 MeV/c² and D∗− mass 2008.6 MeV/c² are used in the two-body production momentum calculation.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Verifies correct mass inputs; untested, supporting detail.

items.title: D* c.m. energy
items.description: The D∗− energy in the c.m. frame is computed as approximately 2080 MeV from √(p² + m²) using mass 2008.6 MeV/c².

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate for the Lorentz boost to the pion; untested but load-bearing.

items.title: D* boost beta
items.description: The velocity parameter β = p/E of the D∗− in the laboratory is computed as approximately 0.26.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required boost parameter for pion momentum; untested but load-bearing.

items.title: D* boost gamma
items.description: The Lorentz factor γ = E/m of the D∗− is computed as approximately 1.036 using its mass 2008.6 MeV/c².

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required boost parameter for pion momentum; untested but load-bearing.

items.title: Pion rest-frame p*
items.description: The pion momentum in the D∗− rest frame is computed as approximately 38.9 MeV/c from two-body decay kinematics and is subsequently boosted to the laboratory frame.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus of rollouts gives p* ≈ 38.8–38.9 MeV/c using the two-body decay formula with m_{D*} = 2008.6 and m_{D̄0} = 1863.3.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gets a different p* due to wrong masses or formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; caught 2/2 negatives (disc 1.00) but gold=FAIL, so lower weight.

validation.gold_why: Rest-frame momentum not stated.

items.title: Pion rest-frame energy
items.description: The pion energy in the D∗− rest frame is computed as approximately 145 MeV from √(p*² + m_π²), using the full energy-momentum relation.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for correct boost: the slow pion has E* ≠ p*, unlike a massless particle.

items.title: Lorentz boost for pion
items.description: The maximum pion laboratory momentum is obtained via the Lorentz boost formula p_max = γ(p* + βE*), applying the D∗− boost to the pion rest-frame quantities.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding momenta across frames': p_D* + p* ≈ 589 MeV/c is wrong by a factor of ~7.
provenance.discriminates: A response that simply sums the D* momentum and the pion rest-frame momentum.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects all intermediates to final 79 MeV/c; caught 0/2 but structurally central.

validation.gold_why: Reports 79, not ~589 MeV/c.

items.title: Pion mass used
items.description: The charged pion mass of approximately 139.6 MeV/c² is used in the decay kinematics and boost calculation, even though it is not given in the problem statement.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Essential input not provided in prompt; untested, supporting detail.

items.title: D0 mass in decay
items.description: The D̄⁰ mass 1863.3 MeV/c² is used in the two-body decay momentum calculation for D∗− → D̄⁰π⁻.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Verifies correct decay mass input; untested, supporting detail.

items.title: Small decay Q-value
items.description: The response notes that the D∗− → D̄⁰π⁻ decay has a small Q-value of approximately 5.7 MeV, making the pion energy primarily rest mass in the D∗− rest frame.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Real physics insight justifying why E* ≫ p*; untested, low weight.

items.title: Avoids massless pion
items.description: Avoids computing the pion laboratory momentum using the ultra-relativistic approximation p_max ≈ γp*(1+β), which incorrectly treats the slow pion as massless by setting E* = p*.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Massless-pion boost formula': γp*(1+β) ≈ 51 MeV/c instead of ~80 MeV/c because E*/p* ≈ 3.7.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the simplified boost γp*(1+β) and gets ~51 MeV/c.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap for this decay; caught 0/2 but names a concrete wrong formula.

validation.gold_why: Reports 79, consistent with full boost.
