items.title: Starting identity
items.description: Uses det(UU†) = det(I) = 1 as the starting identity for a unitary matrix, from which the determinant's unit-modulus property is derived.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference begin from U†U = I, taking det of both sides.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts |det U| = 1 without any derivation or starting identity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but load-bearing intermediate step in the proof.

validation.gold_why: Starts from det(UU†) = det I = 1.

items.title: Product rule step
items.description: Uses the product rule det(UU†) = det U · det U† as an intermediate step in deriving the determinant's unit-modulus property.

provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination; load-bearing intermediate identity connecting steps 1 and 3.

items.title: Conjugate determinant
items.description: States det(U†) = (det U)*, using the dagger property to relate the determinant of the adjoint to the complex conjugate of the determinant.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'det(U†) not conjugated' warns against writing det(U†) = det(U), which forces det U = ±1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes det(U†) = det(U) without conjugation, which would wrongly restrict det U to ±1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but required algebraic identity in the derivation.

validation.gold_why: States det U† = (det U)* explicitly.

items.title: Unit modulus
items.description: States |det U|² = 1, equivalently that the determinant of a unitary matrix has unit modulus, and avoids claiming det U = 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks for the determinant of a general unitary matrix; the reference gives |det U|^2 = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states det U = 0, det U = ±1 only, or gives no modulus constraint.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but core result; correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states |det U|^2 = 1.

items.title: Phase form
items.description: States det U = e^{iα}, where α is a real number, giving the complex phase form of the determinant.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states det U = e^{iα} with α real; all rollouts agreed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes det U = ±1 (losing the general phase) or omits the e^{iα} form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but directly answers sub-question 1's explicit form.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states det U = e^{iα} with α real.

items.title: Exponential determinant
items.description: States det[exp(iF)] = exp(i Tr F) as the explicit determinant of the operator U = exp(iF), where F is a hermitian matrix, and avoids the wrong-sign formula exp(-i Tr F).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks to calculate det explicitly; reference gives det U = exp(i Tr F).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives det[exp(iF)] = Tr(exp(iF)), det = exp(Tr F) without the i, or no explicit formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but the entire point of sub-question 2.

validation.gold_why: States det U = exp(i Tr F) directly.

items.title: Unimodular transform
items.description: States that U' = e^{iα/N} U, where N is the rank of the matrix, gives rise to a unimodular matrix with det U' = 1, and avoids setting c = e^{-iα} without the 1/N factor.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly proves sub-question 3's existence claim; correctness collapses without it.

items.title: Rank identification
items.description: Identifies N as the rank of the matrix in the unimodular transform U' = cU, so that det(cU) = c^N det U = 1.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific identifier from reference; explains why the 1/N exponent appears.

items.title: N-fold ambiguity
items.description: Writes c = e^{-i(α + 2πm)/N} for integer m, expressing the full N-fold ambiguity in det(cU) = 1 for the unimodular transform.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Claiming unique c' notes the correct form includes the integer m indexing the N roots of unity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only c = e^{-iα/N} as a single value without the m-parameterized family of solutions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL; caught 2/2 negatives but over-specifies beyond reference answer.

validation.gold_why: N-fold form with 2πm/N not written.

items.title: Antiphase with unequal amplitudes
items.description: States that the two reflected beams are in antiphase (destructive interference) but have unequal amplitudes, so cancellation is incomplete.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference shows the beams interfere destructively (antiphase) but R₁ ≠ R₂ prevents full cancellation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the beams are not in antiphase, or that equal amplitudes are not required for cancellation.

validation.gold_why: States destructive interference but unequal intensities, incomplete cancellation.

items.title: Avoids one-phase-shift thickness
items.description: Avoids stating the minimum thickness as 5000/(2 × 1.2) ≈ 2083 Å, which would result from counting only one π phase shift at the coating surfaces.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'One phase shift counted' and 'Admits only one phase shift' pitfalls both produce d ≈ 2083 Å.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 2083 Å as the minimum coating thickness.

validation.gold_why: Gives 0.10 μm, not 2083 Å.

items.title: Avoids arithmetic mean index
items.description: Avoids claiming the ideal coating index equals the arithmetic mean (1 + 1.4)/2 = 1.2, which would imply no change is needed.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Arithmetic mean for index' pitfall yields exactly 1.2, creating false confirmation that the given index is already ideal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the given n₁ = 1.2 already satisfies the zero-reflection condition.

validation.gold_why: States ideal index 1.18, not arithmetic mean 1.2.

items.title: Avoids wrong index direction
items.description: Avoids stating that the coating index must increase from 1.2 to achieve zero reflected intensity.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Wrong direction of change' pitfall claims Δn ≈ +0.017 or an increase to 1.217.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the index must increase rather than decrease from 1.2.

validation.gold_why: Ideal index 1.18 is below 1.2, implies decrease.

items.title: Avoids double-dividing wavelength
items.description: Avoids computing the coating thickness as 5000/(4 × 1.2²) ≈ 868 Å by substituting the in-medium wavelength λ/n₁ into the interference condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Forget vacuum wavelength' pitfall double-divides by n₁, giving d = λ/(4n₁²) ≈ 868 Å.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the in-medium wavelength and obtains a thickness near 868 Å.

validation.gold_why: Uses λ/(4n₁), not λ/(4n₁²).

items.title: Five components stated
items.description: The response states that the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines in amorphous solids consists of five components.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts described a three-component structure (central + one Brillouin doublet) rather than the correct five-component structure.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe the spectrum qualitatively without committing to the explicit count of five components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the total count is the load-bearing fact of the answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states five components.

items.title: One undisplaced component
items.description: The response identifies one undisplaced component as part of the fine structure of the Rayleigh scattering lines.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states 'one undisplaced component'; all rollouts mentioned a central peak but the reference frames it as part of a five-component count.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that omit the central elastic peak entirely or fail to label it as one of the five components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core reference content; 0/3 discrimination because flawed responses still included it.

validation.gold_why: Identifies one undisplaced component.

items.title: Two displaced pairs
items.description: The response states that there are two pairs of displaced components in the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states 'two pairs of displaced components'; rollouts described only one pair definitively.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that mention only one displaced pair (longitudinal) and omit the second pair.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the pair structure is a central discriminator.

validation.gold_why: States two pairs of displaced components.

items.title: Transverse acoustic pair
items.description: The response states that the other pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by transverse acoustic waves.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts hedged on or omitted the transverse pair, treating it as optional or geometry-dependent, while the reference states it as a definite second pair.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that treat transverse acoustic scattering as conditional, weak, or geometry-dependent rather than as a definite component of the fine structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the transverse pair is the key challenging fact.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The response states that one pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by longitudinal acoustic waves.

validation.gold_why: Other pair from transverse acoustic waves.

items.title: Qualitative description
items.description: The response describes the fine structure of the Rayleigh light scattering lines qualitatively, without relying on numerical calculations of frequency shifts or intensities.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure notes the implicit constraint that the answer must be qualitative, not numerical.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that attempt numerical calculations of Brillouin shifts instead of providing the requested qualitative description.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests qualitative description; 0/3 discrimination, minor depth.

validation.gold_why: Describes qualitatively in prose.

items.title: Stokes and anti-Stokes
items.description: The response states that each pair of displaced components includes both a Stokes-shifted and an anti-Stokes-shifted component.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Anti-Stokes line dropped' warns against omitting the time-reversed anti-Stokes process.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe one displaced line per phonon branch instead of symmetric pairs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real physics depth beyond terse reference; 0/3 discrimination, low weight.

validation.gold_why: Mentions pairs, does not drop anti-Stokes.

items.title: Transverse pair definite
items.description: Avoids describing the transverse acoustic displaced pair as present only under certain sample geometries rather than as a definite component of the five-component structure in amorphous solids.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Transverse pair omitted' was observed in all rollouts, which hedged on transverse components.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that frame transverse Brillouin components as conditional or weak rather than intrinsic.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; discounted for structural pitfall advantage.

validation.gold_why: Treats transverse pair as definite component.

items.title: Avoids crystal selection rules
items.description: Avoids applying crystalline momentum-conservation selection rules that would forbid or strongly suppress transverse acoustic scattering in amorphous solids.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Crystal selection rules applied' warns against uncritically carrying over crystal selection rules to glasses.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim only longitudinal modes contribute based on crystalline backscattering selection rules.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; discounted for structural advantage, less central than count.

validation.gold_why: Does not apply crystal selection rules.

items.title: Longitudinal acoustic pair
items.description: The response states that one pair of displaced components is obtained from scattering by longitudinal acoustic waves.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly identified a longitudinal acoustic Brillouin doublet.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that fail to attribute any displaced pair to longitudinal acoustic waves.

validation.gold_why: One pair from longitudinal acoustic waves.

items.title: Names extinction
items.description: The response identifies extinction as the psychological process that best explains why the patient stopped crying before physician visits.

provenance.evidence_detail: The single required deliverable is naming the psychological process; the reference and all rollouts identify extinction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names habituation, counterconditioning, desensitization, or forgetting instead of extinction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 flawed responses; naming the correct process is the core answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly names extinction as the process.

items.title: Non-reinforced exposure mechanism
items.description: The response explains that extinction occurs because repeated physician visits no longer produced the expected negative outcome, weakening the conditioned association.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'the expected negative outcome no longer occurs' and 'this association weakened.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that names extinction but does not link it to repeated visits without aversive consequences.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; key underlying mechanism linking visits to extinction.

validation.gold_why: Explains extinction occurs because expected negative outcome no longer occurs.

items.title: Extinction defined
items.description: The response defines extinction as the process by which a conditioned response diminishes because the expected negative outcome no longer occurs.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'Extinction occurs when the conditioned response, in this case, the crying, diminishes because the expected negative outcome no longer occurs.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that names extinction without stating what the process entails.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; formal definition anchors the correct psychological concept.

validation.gold_why: Defines extinction as CR diminishing because expected outcome no longer occurs.

items.title: Visits became routine
items.description: The response states that physician visits became routine and devoid of negative experiences over time.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'as the visits became routine and devoid of negative experiences,' language no rollout used.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains extinction mechanistically but omits the temporal/familiarity dimension of visits becoming routine.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; vignette-anchored fact essential to the extinction account.

validation.gold_why: States visits became routine and devoid of negative experiences.

items.title: Crying developed through associations
items.description: The response states that the child's crying was a conditioned response developed through negative associations with prior medical experiences.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference describes crying as a conditioned response arising from an association between doctor visits and negative experiences.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names extinction but treats crying as an innate reflex or an operant behavior rather than a learned conditioned response.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2; explains the acquisition phase of the conditioned crying.

validation.gold_why: States crying developed from negative associations with medical experiences.

items.title: Fear reduced
items.description: The response states that the child's fear of physician visits has been reduced, leading to the cessation of crying behavior.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference concludes: 'the child's fear of doctor visits has reduced, leading to the cessation of the crying behavior.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies extinction but does not connect the process to the emotional outcome of reduced fear.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2; clinically relevant emotional outcome of extinction.

validation.gold_why: States child's fear reduced, leading to cessation of crying.

items.title: CR identified as crying
items.description: The response identifies the crying behavior as the conditioned response that diminished through extinction.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus claim states: 'crying (CR)' is the conditioned response that diminishes during extinction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names extinction but does not specify which behavior was the conditioned response.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; specific identification adds precision to the extinction explanation.

validation.gold_why: Identifies crying as the conditioned response.

items.title: Association weakened over time
items.description: The response states that the association between physician visits and negative experiences weakened over time as the conditioned response diminished.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'Over time... this association weakened.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that states extinction occurred but does not describe the weakening of the prior association.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; describes the temporal weakening of the conditioned association.

validation.gold_why: States association weakened over time.

items.title: Mechanism linkage to vignette
items.description: The response connects extinction to the specific scenario by stating that the child continued attending physician visits and the expected negative outcome no longer occurred.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unanswered mechanism linkage' (severity low) warns that a bare label 'extinction' without mapping to conditioning elements is insufficient.
provenance.discriminates: A response that provides only the bare label 'extinction' with no connection to the physician-visit scenario.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; links extinction theory to this patient's situation.

validation.gold_why: States child continued visits and negative outcome no longer occurred.

items.title: Avoids operant framing
items.description: Avoids framing the crying as an operant behavior reinforced by attention or escape, and instead identifies the process as classical (Pavlovian) extinction of a conditioned fear response.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Operant extinction confusion' warns that crying can be misread as an operant behavior maintained by attention.
provenance.discriminates: A response that labels the process as operant extinction or claims crying was previously reinforced by attention.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2; central distinction between operant and classical conditioning.

validation.gold_why: Frames as classical extinction, no operant framing present.

items.title: Avoids habituation label
items.description: Avoids naming habituation as the psychological process, instead identifying extinction as the weakening of the learned conditioned crying response.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Habituation vs extinction' (severity high) warns that habituation sounds plausible but applies to unconditioned responses, not learned fear associations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'habituation,' treating the diminished crying as a decreased innate response rather than weakening of a conditioned response.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2; distinguishes extinction from habituation, a common error.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention habituation; names extinction.

items.title: Avoids counterconditioning label
items.description: Avoids naming counterconditioning as the psychological process, since the cessation occurred without the promise of rewards and without pairing the feared stimulus with a new positive association.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Counterconditioning claim' (severity high) warns that counterconditioning requires an active positive replacement, which the vignette rules out.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'counterconditioning,' implying a new positive association was formed to replace the negative one.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2; absence of rewards in the vignette rules out counterconditioning.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention counterconditioning.

items.title: Fetal renal abnormality
items.description: Identifies a fetal renal abnormality as the condition most likely associated with the reduced amniotic fluid volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: The single labelled sub-question asks for the most likely associated condition; the reference answer names fetal renal abnormality as the answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names placental insufficiency, maternal dehydration, or post-term pregnancy instead of a fetal renal cause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; caught 2/2 negatives, perfect discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Identifies fetal renal abnormality as most likely cause.

items.title: Categorical renal term
items.description: Uses the term 'renal abnormality' or equivalent categorical language for the fetal condition, rather than relying solely on a single named diagnosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses broader language ('renal abnormality in the fetus'); the 'Category vs. single entity' pitfall notes this distinction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names only bilateral renal agenesis without acknowledging the broader category of fetal renal abnormalities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; adds specificity beyond naming one diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: Uses 'renal abnormality' as categorical language.

items.title: Bilateral renal agenesis
items.description: Names bilateral renal agenesis as a specific condition causing the reduced amniotic fluid volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on specificity; the reference explicitly names bilateral renal agenesis as a cause.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions only a vague 'kidney problem' without naming bilateral renal agenesis or a comparable specific fetal renal entity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference-named condition; caught 2/2 negatives with high discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Names bilateral renal agenesis explicitly.

items.title: Urinary tract obstruction
items.description: Names urinary tract obstructions as a co-equal cause of the reduced amniotic fluid alongside bilateral renal agenesis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference presents urinary tract obstructions as a co-equal cause; rollouts mentioned obstructions only in differentials, if at all.
provenance.discriminates: A response limited solely to bilateral renal agenesis that omits urinary tract obstruction as a qualifying cause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference-named condition; caught 2/2 negatives with high discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Names urinary tract obstructions alongside renal agenesis.

items.title: Fetal urine as source
items.description: States that at 30 weeks the fetus contributes to amniotic fluid volume through urine production.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that fetal urine is the major source at 30 weeks; the reference anchors the answer to this physiology.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct diagnosis without any physiological linkage to fetal urine production at 30 weeks.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key physiology; caught 1/2 negatives, moderate discrimination.

validation.gold_why: States fetus contributes to fluid via urine production.

items.title: Impeded urine mechanism
items.description: Explains that bilateral renal agenesis or urinary tract obstructions impede fetal urine output, leading to oligohydramnios.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states that these conditions impede fetal urine output, leading to oligohydramnios.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the condition but does not connect it mechanistically to reduced fetal urine output.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Causal mechanism linking condition to outcome; caught 2/2 negatives from source 6.

validation.gold_why: Explains these conditions impede urine output causing oligohydramnios.

items.title: 30-weeks anchors reasoning
items.description: Explicitly references the 30 weeks gestational age as the reason fetal urine production is the dominant contributor to amniotic fluid volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference anchors its answer to the 30-week physiology; the implicit_constraints note this gestational age dependency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct diagnosis but does not tie the reasoning to the specific gestational age of 30 weeks.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Temporal reasoning anchor; caught 2/2 negatives, high discrimination.

validation.gold_why: References 30 weeks as when fetal urine contributes significantly.

items.title: Fetal not maternal cause
items.description: Identifies the associated condition as fetal in origin rather than a maternal condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed the cause is fetal/renal; the reference consistently frames the answer as a fetal condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the low AFI primarily to a maternal condition rather than a fetal renal abnormality.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes correct fetal etiology; caught 2/2 negatives, high discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Identifies condition as fetal in origin, not maternal.

items.title: Avoids post-term pregnancy
items.description: Avoids selecting post-term pregnancy as the associated condition, which is impossible at 30 weeks of gestation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Post-term as cause' with high severity; post-term is a classic exam distractor but impossible at 30 weeks.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names post-term pregnancy (≥41 weeks) as the cause of the low AFI at 30 weeks.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific impossible-at-30-weeks trap; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Does not select post-term pregnancy.

items.title: Avoids polyhydramnios causes
items.description: Avoids selecting a cause of polyhydramnios such as maternal diabetes, fetal GI obstruction, or neural tube defect as the associated condition for the low AFI.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Polyhydramnios cause selected' with high severity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names maternal diabetes, anencephaly, or GI obstruction as the cause of reduced amniotic fluid.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Opposite-condition trap; caught 1/2 negatives, moderate discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Does not select polyhydramnios causes.

items.title: Selects option A, F
items.description: Selects option A and names F as the sound most affected when teeth in the anterior maxilla are set too far down anteriorly.

provenance.discriminates: A response that names the labiodental class but hedges between F and V or arbitrarily picks V.

items.title: F relies on lip-teeth interaction
items.description: States that the F sound relies on interaction between the upper teeth and the lower lip.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollout attempts and the reference agree that F depends on lower-lip-to-maxillary-incisal-edge contact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the answer without mentioning the upper-teeth-to-lower-lip contact mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Anatomical basis for F production; caught 0/2 but essential reasoning.

validation.gold_why: States F relies on upper teeth and lower lip interaction.

items.title: Lower lip friction on upper teeth
items.description: States that the lower lip must create friction against the upper teeth to produce the F sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes friction between upper teeth and lower lip as necessary for F production.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions lip-tooth contact but does not specify friction as the mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specifies the friction mechanism; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States lower lip creates friction against upper teeth for F.

items.title: Misalignment alters airflow
items.description: States that misalignment alters the airflow needed to produce a clear F sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states that suboptimal positioning alters the airflow needed to produce a clear F sound.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the mechanism via contact alone without mentioning altered airflow.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the causal chain; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States misalignment alters airflow needed for F.

items.title: Suboptimal positioning disrupts balance
items.description: Explains that suboptimal positioning of the anterior teeth disrupts the delicate balance needed for the F sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states that suboptimal positioning can disrupt a delicate balance, altering the airflow for F.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks F without explaining why positioning matters for the sound.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links positioning to sound production; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States suboptimal positioning alters delicate balance for F.

items.title: F is unvoiced fricative
items.description: Identifies F as an unvoiced fricative sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes F as an 'unvoiced fricative'; rollouts did not use this term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly picks F but does not specify its phonetic class.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added phonetic depth; caught 1/2 negatives, discrimination 0.50.

validation.gold_why: Identifies F as an unvoiced fricative.

items.title: Avoids selecting V
items.description: Avoids selecting option B (V) as the correct answer.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: candidates may pick V over F because both are labiodental consonants.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects V instead of F, treating both labiodental sounds as equally affected.
provenance.calibration_rationale: V is the closest labiodental distractor; caught 1/2 negatives.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Avoids selecting option D (S) as the correct answer.

validation.gold_why: Does not select option B.

items.title: Final concentration value
items.description: States the initial concentration of copper sulphate as 9.6×10⁻⁵ M.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to calculate the initial CuSO4 concentration and select the matching option; the reference answer gives 9.6×10⁻⁵ M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects any other numeric value, e.g. 4.8×10⁻⁵ M or 1.2×10⁻⁵ M.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final answer is the core deliverable.

validation.gold_why: States 9.6×10⁻⁵ M as final answer.

items.title: Current unit conversion
items.description: Converts the given current of 2 mA to 2×10⁻³ A before computing charge.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'mA not converted to amperes' identifies using I = 2 directly as a common error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 2 instead of 2×10⁻³ in the charge calculation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; necessary unit conversion for correct charge.

validation.gold_why: Uses 2×10⁻³ A in the charge calculation.

items.title: Time unit conversion
items.description: Multiplies 19.3 min by 60 to obtain the electrolysis duration in seconds as 1158 s.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Minutes not converted to seconds' identifies using 19.3 directly as a common error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs 19.3 directly into Q = I·t without the ×60 conversion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; necessary unit conversion for correct charge.

validation.gold_why: Multiplies 19.3 by 60 in the charge calculation.

items.title: Total charge passed
items.description: Computes total charge Q = 2×10⁻³ × 19.3 × 60 ≈ 2.316 C passed through the copper sulphate solution.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on Q = 2.316 C; this is a load-bearing intermediate value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that arrives at a charge value differing by a factor of 60 or 1000 due to unit errors.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; load-bearing intermediate in the Faraday calculation chain.

validation.gold_why: Shows Q = 2×10⁻³ × 19.3 × 60 in the computation.

items.title: Faraday constant division
items.description: Divides charge Q by the Faraday constant 96500 to obtain moles of electrons.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts used 96485 and the reference used 96500; both are acceptable and yield the same result to the required precision.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips the Faraday constant division entirely or uses an unrelated constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination; required step converting charge to moles of electrons.

validation.gold_why: Divides Q by 96500 to get moles of electrons.

items.title: Applies 50% absorbance relation
items.description: Uses the 50% absorbance reduction to conclude that half the original copper was removed, so initial moles equal 2 × 1.2×10⁻⁵ = 2.4×10⁻⁵ mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Dropping 50% absorbance factor' identifies treating removed moles as the full initial amount; the reference shows multiplying by 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats 1.2×10⁻⁵ mol as the total initial amount rather than only half of it.

validation.gold_why: Multiplies 1.2×10⁻⁵ by 2 for initial moles.

items.title: Names transference
items.description: The response identifies the situation as transference in which the patient projects feelings onto the therapist, with the direction of feelings flowing from patient to therapist rather than from therapist to patient.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Countertransference mislabel' pitfall is high severity and foreseen; reversing the direction is a common error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that calls the phenomenon countertransference instead of transference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core concept; measured 0.50 discrimination across two absorbed sources.

validation.gold_why: Does not label patient's feelings as countertransference.

items.title: Names idealization
items.description: The response identifies idealization as a mechanism alongside transference, characterizing the patient's belief that the therapist deeply understands their emotions as an idealized distortion rather than a realistic appraisal of the therapeutic relationship.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Genuine rapport framing' pitfall is high severity; the reference explicitly frames the perception as mistaken and a distortion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that frames the patient's perception as accurate empathy or healthy therapeutic rapport.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Second key mechanism; absorbed the genuine-rapport pitfall for direction.

validation.gold_why: Describes misinterpretation as idealized distortion, not realistic appraisal.

items.title: Projects past relationships
items.description: The response explains that transference involves feelings and attitudes that originate from early relationships with significant figures such as parents or caregivers.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference describes transference as projecting feelings originating from early relationships with caregivers, a detail the rollouts partially addressed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines transference generically without specifying the historical/relational origin of the projected feelings.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines transference mechanism; reference-grounded, no negatives caught.

validation.gold_why: Explains transference originates from early relationships with caregivers.

items.title: Positive or negative pole
items.description: The response notes that transference can involve positive or negative feelings projected onto the therapist, with the affectionate feelings in this case representing the positive pole.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference describes transference feelings as positive or negative, providing the affective context for the affectionate presentation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies transference is exclusively positive or exclusively negative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Strongest measured signal: caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Notes transference feelings can be positive or negative.

items.title: Correct formula used
items.description: The response uses the formula ΔS = nR ln(V₂/V₁) for the reversible isothermal expansion of one mole of an ideal gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires calculating ΔS; the consensus correct approach uses this formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong or absent formula, such as computing nR×(V₂/V₁) without a logarithm.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; the core formula without which the answer cannot be correct.

validation.gold_why: Uses nR ln(V₂/V₁) via nR ln 2.00.

items.title: Volume ratio 2.00
items.description: The response forms the volume ratio V₂/V₁ = 20.0/10.0 = 2.00, not the inverted ratio 10.0/20.0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct value from all rollouts and the reference; the ratio 2.00 is load-bearing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the ratio to 10.0/20.0 or uses a different ratio.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; correct ratio is load-bearing for the entire calculation.

validation.gold_why: Implies ratio 2.00 from 20.0/10.0.

items.title: Natural logarithm applied
items.description: The response applies the natural logarithm ln to the ratio 2.00, yielding ln(2.00) ≈ 0.6931, not the base-10 logarithm.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'log10 instead of ln' (high severity); also 'ln omitted entirely'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses log₁₀(2.00) or skips the logarithm entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; using log₁₀ or omitting ln produces a numerically wrong ΔS.

validation.gold_why: Applies ln to 2.00, yielding ln 2.00.

items.title: Correct R value
items.description: The response uses R = 8.314 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹, not R = 0.08206 dm³·atm·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹, in the calculation of ΔS for one mole of ideal gas expanded isothermally.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong R units' (medium severity); consensus correct uses 8.314 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses R = 0.08206 dm³·atm·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹ without converting to joules.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; wrong R units yield a value orders of magnitude off.

validation.gold_why: Uses R implicitly, gets 5.76 J·K⁻¹.

items.title: Final ΔS with units

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) target; consensus correct final value from all rollouts and the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a different numerical value such as 2.50, 16.63, or −5.76.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question specifies one mole of ideal gas; consensus correct uses n = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different value of n or drops n from the formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00 but necessary for the correct numeric result; untested by flaws.

items.title: Derivation from δq = PdV
items.description: The response derives ΔS starting from δq = PdV for the isothermal process of the ideal gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference-only content: the reference shows the step-by-step derivation from first principles; all rollouts jump straight to the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only writes the final formula without any thermodynamic derivation.

items.title: Integral form of ΔS
items.description: The response writes the integral form ΔS = ∫(δq_rev/T) = ∫(P/T)dV before evaluating it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference-only content: the reference explicitly writes the integral form before substituting the ideal gas equation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips directly to the integrated result without showing the integral.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00; shows the formal thermodynamic step linking heat to entropy.

items.title: Ideal gas substitution
items.description: The response substitutes P = nRT/V from the ideal gas equation to obtain ΔS = ∫(nR/V)dV.

items.title: Avoids omitting logarithm

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00 in tests but names a specific arithmetic error yielding 16.63.

validation.gold_why: Includes ln, doesn't skip it.

items.title: Work-energy framework
items.description: The response frames the problem using work-energy, stating that the integral of force over distance (∫F dx) equals the kinetic energy that must be dissipated.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used impulse-momentum (maximize Δt) as the primary framework; the reference uses work-energy (∫F dx = mv₀²/2) and explicitly calls the momentum approach trickier.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only uses F_avg = Δp/Δt and never mentions spreading force over distance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core physics principle; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Frames problem via ∫F dx equaling kinetic energy mv₀²/2.

items.title: Force spread evenly
items.description: The response states that to reduce injury the force should be spread out evenly over the largest possible crumpling distance rather than spiked over a small interval, and that choice (b) achieves this because the front crumples when large forces are applied.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts maximized collision time; the reference argues the goal is to spread F over the largest possible range of x.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the goal is only to maximize collision duration without mentioning spreading force over distance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central design principle; both sources caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States force should spread evenly over largest possible x range.

items.title: ∫F dx fixed value
items.description: The response states that the integral ∫F dx is fixed at the magnitude mv₀²/2 because the occupant ends at rest, independent of the specifics of the collision.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states this integral takes on the given value mv₀²/2 in magnitude, independent of collision specifics; no rollout mentioned this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the total energy or force integral as variable depending on design.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate result; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: States ∫F dx fixed at mv₀²/2, independent of collision specifics.

items.title: Option (a) bumper limited
items.description: The response explains that option (a) involves only the front bumper, which is a small fraction of the total possible crumpling distance, making it hardly different from a completely rigid car.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference distinguishes (a) from (d) by noting the bumper is only a small fraction of crumpling distance; all rollouts lumped (a) and (d) together.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats (a) and (d) as identical rigid designs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required sub-question coverage; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Explains (a) involves only bumper, small fraction of crumpling distance.

items.title: Option (c) spikes at end
items.description: The response explains that option (c) leads to a force spike at the end of the collision because the front crumples easily under small forces, providing little deceleration early on.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'missing spike-timing analysis' pitfall: rollouts said rigid or poor designs cause high force without specifying when the spike happens.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions high force for wrong options but never specifies the timing of the spike within the collision.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific spike-timing analysis; caught 2/3 negatives, discrimination 0.67.

validation.gold_why: Specifies (c) spikes at end, (d) spikes at beginning.

items.title: Option (d) spikes at beginning
items.description: The response explains that option (d) leads to a force spike at the beginning of the collision because the completely rigid front does not crumple at all to absorb energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'missing spike-timing analysis' pitfall: rollouts said rigid or poor designs cause high force without specifying when the spike happens.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions high force for wrong options but never specifies the timing of the spike within the collision.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific spike-timing analysis; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Specifies (c) spikes at end, (d) spikes at beginning.

items.title: Option (e) repeats process
items.description: The response explains that option (e) is inferior because the springs throw the occupant backward after stopping, causing the whole deceleration process to be repeated and making injury more likely.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts argued (e) doubles Δp; the reference argues springs throw you backward, repeating the process.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only argues (e) doubles the momentum change without mentioning process repetition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key mechanism for rejecting (e); caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Explains springs throw occupant backward, repeating the process.

items.title: Spring force non-uniform
items.description: The response notes that the spring force in option (e) is not uniform, so it somewhat spikes halfway through the process when compression is maximal.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states the spring force isn't uniform and somewhat spikes halfway through; no rollout mentioned this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats spring force as constant or only discusses total impulse change.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth on spring mechanics; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Notes spring force isn't uniform, spikes halfway through.

items.title: Time maximization insufficient
items.description: The response explains that maximizing collision time alone does not prevent injury because one could suddenly decelerate to a small speed and continue forward, which would injure the occupant.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's remark notes that time has no maximum and one could decelerate to a small speed then coast, but this sudden deceleration injures; no rollout engaged this subtlety.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims maximizing collision time is always the correct goal without qualification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real depth on momentum approach; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Explains long time alone fails; sudden deceleration to small speed injures.

items.title: Distance constrained, not time
items.description: The response notes that the crumple zone constrains the maximum possible distance over which the collision occurs but does not constrain time, making the work-energy framework the natural choice.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's remark explains the momentum approach is trickier because the collision has a specific maximum possible distance but no maximum possible time.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats time and distance as equally constrained by the crumple zone.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies framework choice; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Notes collision has max distance but no max possible time.

items.title: Constant force is ideal
items.description: The response identifies that the ideal force function F(t) during the collision is a constant function, which minimizes the maximum value of force.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's remark states the answer is that you want F(t) to be a constant function to minimize the maximum value of F.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the ideal force profile has any shape other than constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects to optimization insight; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Identifies constant F(t) as ideal to minimize maximum force.

items.title: Avoids structural-integrity argument
items.description: Avoids justifying the rejection of option (c) by citing collapse during normal driving or loss of structural integrity, and instead addresses the physics of a force spike at the end of the collision.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts argued (c) fails due to structural integrity during normal driving; the reference gives the physics reason that (c) causes a force spike at the end of the collision.
provenance.discriminates: A response that rejects (c) using only practical engineering concerns rather than force-profile physics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed divergent error; caught 2/3 negatives, discrimination 0.67.

validation.gold_why: Rejects (c) via force-spike-at-end physics, not structural integrity.

items.title: Avoids doubled-momentum claim
items.description: Avoids justifying the rejection of option (e) solely by claiming the momentum change doubles from +mv to −mv, and instead addresses the mechanism of process repetition and non-uniform spring force.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts argued (e) is bad because Δp doubles; the reference argues springs repeat the process and the non-uniform force spikes halfway through.
provenance.discriminates: A response that rejects (e) only with the doubled-Δp textbook simplification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed divergent error; caught 2/3 negatives, discrimination 0.67.

validation.gold_why: Rejects (e) via process repetition and non-uniform spring force.

items.title: Avoids conflating (a) and (d)
items.description: Avoids treating options (a) and (d) as identical by noting that (a) involves only the front bumper, a small fraction of the total crumpling distance, while (d) is completely rigid.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts lumped (a) and (d) together as 'rigid front'; the reference distinguishes them because (a) is only the bumper.
provenance.discriminates: A response that groups (a) and (d) together without distinguishing the bumper-only case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed conflation error; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Distinguishes (a) bumper-only from (d) completely rigid.

items.title: Final formula for dS
items.description: The response derives the final result \(dS = \frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\) for the two-compartment system with a flexible wall, with no residual \(dU\) term and the common temperature \(T\) in the denominator.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) target is the stated expression for dS.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives an intermediate but never writes the target expression, or writes a sign-flipped version such as \((P_A - P_B)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result of the problem; caught 2/2 negatives. Merging in items 15 and 19 removes redundant restatements of the same formula.

validation.gold_why: Final result stated explicitly.

items.title: Per-subsystem entropy relation
items.description: The response writes \(dS_i = \frac{1}{T}(dU_i + P_i dV_i)\) or equivalently \(dU_i = T\,dS_i - P_i dV_i\) for each compartment.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts began from this fundamental relation for each subsystem.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong sign, e.g. \(dS_i = (1/T)(dU_i - P_i dV_i)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate identity; caught 1/2 negatives (0.50 discrimination).

validation.gold_why: Per-subsystem entropy relation written.

items.title: First-law heat expression
items.description: The response writes \(\delta q_A = dU_A + P_A dV_A\) and \(\delta q_B = dU_B + P_B dV_B\) via the First Law before forming the entropy differential.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses the First Law and δq/T path rather than jumping to the fundamental relation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the explicit First-Law heat terms but still reaches the formula correctly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Preliminary step feeding item 2; caught 1/2 negatives (0.50). Lower weight as it is upstream of the key identity.

validation.gold_why: First-law heat expressions written.

items.title: Total entropy as sum
items.description: The response writes the total entropy change of the isolated system as \(dS = dS_A + dS_B\) before substituting the per-subsystem relations.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts formed the total entropy as the sum of the two subsystem entropies.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats dS as a single-subsystem quantity rather than the composite system entropy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Genuine intermediate step but 0/2 discrimination; low weight reflects lack of measured signal.

validation.gold_why: dS = dS_A + dS_B written.

items.title: Volume conservation constraint
items.description: The response uses the constraint \(dV_A = -dV_B\) from the flexible wall separating the two subsystems, rather than setting \(dV_A = +dV_B\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Volume conservation sign yields a spurious pressure-sum term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes \(dV_A = dV_B\) and cannot reach the target expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key constraint yielding the pressure difference; caught 1/2 negatives. Absorbs avoidance item 11 which restates this positively.

validation.gold_why: Uses dV_A = -dV_B.

items.title: Isolated system & energy
items.description: The response identifies the two-compartment system as isolated and applies \(dU_A = -dU_B\) so that internal-energy terms cancel in \(dS\).

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts enforced conservation of total internal energy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves a spurious \(dU_A + dU_B\) term in the entropy expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary for the \(dU\) cancellation; 0/2 discrimination so kept at low weight. Merges generic isolated-system statement with the specific constraint.

validation.gold_why: dU_A = -dU_B applied.

items.title: Equal temperatures used
items.description: The response uses \(T_A = T_B = T\) for the two subsystems having the same temperature.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts set the common temperature before simplifying dS.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps separate \(T_A, T_B\) and cannot reduce to the single-T form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required to factor out \(T\); 0/2 discrimination but correctness depends on it, so weight 2.

validation.gold_why: T_A = T_B stated.

items.title: Interpretation P_B > P_A
items.description: The response states that when \(P_B > P_A\), compartment B expands and \(dV_B\) is positive, because \(dS\) must be greater than zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Reversed physical interpretation of the sign of dV_B.
provenance.discriminates: A response with the correct formula but a backwards direction of expansion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers a sub-question; caught 1/2 negatives. Absorbs avoidance item 13 covering reversed interpretation.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The response states that when \(P_B < P_A\), compartment A expands and \(dV_B\) is negative, again because \(dS\) must be greater than zero.

validation.gold_why: Interpretation ties expansion to larger pressure.

items.title: Second-law justification
items.description: The response justifies the signs of \(dV_B\) by invoking the Second Law requirement \(dS \geq 0\) for the isolated system.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts used the second-law entropy-production constraint to fix the sign of dV_B.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the signs without any entropy-positivity argument.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Provides the physical reasoning for the interpretation; 0/2 discrimination so kept at low weight.

validation.gold_why: Invokes dS must be greater than zero.

items.title: Sign consistency check
items.description: The response makes the sign of \(dV_B\) in each case consistent with \(dS \geq 0\) and the sign of \(P_B - P_A\) in the derived expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergence on strict vs non-strict inequality; the reference requires the sign to follow from dS positivity.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose stated signs of \(dV_B\) would make dS negative for a spontaneous process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives (1.00 discrimination); captures global logical consistency across both interpretive cases.

validation.gold_why: Sign of dV_B consistent with dS > 0.

items.title: Avoid reversed work sign
items.description: Avoids writing \(\delta q = dU - P\,dV\) with reversed work sign; rather, the derivation uses \(\delta q = dU + P\,dV\) so that \(dS = \frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\) rather than \(P_A - P_B\).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: Work sign convention produces a sign-reversed pressure difference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the opposite work convention and obtains \(dS = (dV_B/T)(P_A - P_B)\).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific sign error observed in flawed responses; caught 1/2 negatives (0.50). Pitfall of moderate severity.

validation.gold_why: Uses δq = dU + P dV.

items.title: Pressure difference drives change
items.description: The response states that the direction of volume change is driven by the pressure difference \(P_B - P_A\) between the two subsystems.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts tied the sign of dV_B to the pressure-difference factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the volume change to a temperature difference rather than a pressure difference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds physical depth; caught 1/2 negatives (0.50) but largely implied by items 8–9.

validation.gold_why: Pressure difference drives volume change implied.

items.description: Substitutes n = mass divided by molar mass into the equation PV = nRT, producing the form PV = mass times RT divided by molar mass.

items.title: Rearrange for mass/volume
items.description: Rearranges the equation to isolate mass divided by volume on one side.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference shows the step w/V = Pm/(RT); all rollouts produce the equivalent m/V = PM/(RT).
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes n = m/M but leaves the equation in the form PV = (m/M)RT without isolating the density term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step; 1/2 discrimination, bridges substitution to density.

items.title: Identify mass/volume as density
items.description: Identifies mass per unit volume as density within the derivation.

items.title: Density expression Pm/RT
items.description: Arrives at the expression density equals pressure P times molar mass divided by RT, with pressure P and molar mass in the numerator and RT in the denominator.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Inverted algebra' pitfall can swap molar mass to the denominator; the correct result places it in the numerator with P.

items.title: Proportionality for given gas

items.title: Molar mass constant for gas

items.title: States constant temperature

items.title: Substitutes part (a)

items.title: Part (b) final result
items.description: Arrives at \(\ln \gamma_{\pm} = -\left(\frac{v_+ q_+^2 + v_- q_-^2}{v_+ + v_-}\right)\frac{\kappa}{8\pi \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r k_B T}\) as the result of substituting into the gamma formula.
